Q: How can I see a long layout in preview in Android Studio? A:

If you put your layouts in a ScrollView, it should automatically (at least in Android Studio) show you everything.

Another workaround is to make a new AVD file with a high resolution, something like 4000 pixels height, and use that for preview. It worked for me :)

Q: Maven build errors for java app referencing org.controlsfx A:

JavaFX runtime components are missing, you are didn't include them on the modulepath. Use the following comand to point to your JavaFX component library location:

--module-path "/path/to/javafx-sdk/lib" --add-modules javafx.controls,javafx.fxml

Q: python console tab completion not working in windows A:

The original pyreadline (as recommended by the accepted answer) is no longer maintained and doesn't work on newer versions of Python (>=3.10). Installing pyreadline3 works:

python -m pip install pyreadline3

Q: How can I get the number of files in a folder as a variable? A:

A short and sweet method which also ignores symbolic linked directories:

count=$(ls -l | grep ^- | wc -l)

Or if you have a target:

count=$(ls -l /path/to/target | grep ^- | wc -l)

Q: InvalidInstanceId: An error occurred (InvalidInstanceId) when calling the SendCommand operation A:

I had this issue with an AWS EC2 instance that was working fine previously with Amazon SSM.

I got the error when I tried to run my GitLab pipeline:

An error occurred (InvalidInstanceId) when calling the SendCommand operation: Instances [[i-078d0der4a16e4502]] not in a valid state for account 321403451707

Here's how I fixed it:

  • I checked the IAM permissions, and it already had the SecretsManagerReadWrite policy attached to the EC2 IAM role. And the pipeline has been working fine.

  • I was also sure that the SSM agent was installed on the EC2 previously which is the reason why the pipeline was working fine before.

  • The instance ID was also correct, and I double-checked it again just to be sure that there was no mistake.

All I had to do was restart the EC2 instance just like Elmaquinista suggested above and then tried running the pipeline again.

This time, it worked fine.
